title: Inverse image on the localizing categories
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p$ and $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p$. Let $Y,Y'$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ a $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be admissible: a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $\mathcal O_E$ is its valuation ring. Use the condensed coefficient sheaves, unbounded derived categories, and small direct sums of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use specifically the condensed ring of continuous maps valued in some finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Write $\Dctf$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and $\Loc$ for their localizing closure [sk-def-localizing-closure].

The inverse image $g^*=Lg^*:D(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)\to D(Y'_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] is exact as a triangulated functor [def-weil-triangulated-category], preserves arbitrary small direct sums, maps $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y',\Lambda)$, and hence restricts to an exact sum-preserving functor $\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y',\Lambda))$.

proof.text: *Exactness and sums.* By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], the coefficient map $g^{-1}\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_{Y'}$ is invertible and the module inverse image is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to this exact functor: its termwise functor descends to a triangulated functor on the unbounded derived categories. For any K-flat resolution $P\to K$, exactness makes the termwise map $g^*P\to g^*K$ a quasi-isomorphism. The resolution computation in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] therefore identifies this descended functor with the total derived pullback $Lg^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. The latter node supplies $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$, so [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] gives preservation of every existing small coproduct. Such coproducts exist here: module objects over the commutative coefficient ring are ordinary sheaves of modules, hence form a Grothendieck abelian category by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]; [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts] supplies the small derived coproducts, including the empty one. The small sites are taken in the fixed universe of [sk-def-localizing-closure].

*Finite-coefficient constructibility and Tor amplitude.* Let $A$ be finite and killed by a power of $\ell$, and $K\in\Dctf(Y,A)$. By [lem-sfb-dc-upper-star-preserves], $Lg^*K$ is bounded constructible: $g$ is a morphism of the field setting in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Choose $a\le b$ bounding the Tor amplitude of $K$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. We realize the source's flat-model argument by the general bounded-flat-model construction, valid over the stated field $k$. On the ringed site $(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},A_Y)$, [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] give an additive symmetric closed monoidal Grothendieck category of modules. The functorial bounded-above flat replacements of [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement], applied to $M[0]$ with upper bound zero, give a functor $F$ with flat values and a natural epimorphism $F(M)\to M$. Set $M_0=M$ and $M_{r+1}=\ker(F(M_r)\to M_r)$ for $r\ge0$. The differential $F(M_{r+1})\to F(M_r)$ is the composite through $M_{r+1}\hookrightarrow F(M_r)$; the resulting augmented complex is exact, and naturality and functoriality of kernels give functorial flat resolutions. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-sc-source-tor-amplitude-flat-model] hold, and it gives $K\cong Q(P)$ with flat $P^i$ and $P^i=0$ outside $[a,b]$. By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], $P$ is K-flat. The morphism of pro-étale topoi [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], together with the coefficient isomorphism of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], is a morphism of ringed topoi, so [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] says that $g^*P$ is K-flat with flat terms. Exactness from step 1 makes $Q(g^*P)$ represent $Lg^*K$, and its terms still vanish outside $[a,b]$. The reverse implication of the flat-model criterion [lem-sc-source-tor-amplitude-flat-model] is not needed: directly, K-flat derived tensor is computed by tensoring a K-flat argument [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For any $A_{Y'}$-module sheaf $N$, $Lg^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}N[0]$ is represented by the ordinary complex with terms $g^*P^i\otimes N$. These terms vanish outside $[a,b]$, so its cohomology vanishes there. This tests every sheaf $N$ on $Y'$, and proves finite Tor amplitude. Together with bounded constructibility it proves $Lg^*K\in\Dctf(Y',A)$.

*Integral and field coefficients.* For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] identifies $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ with $\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ for $T=Y,Y'$. Both schemes are qcqs: finite type of their structure maps means that they are quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], since the base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine; quasi-separatedness follows from separatedness because the diagonal is a closed immersion, hence proper and quasi-compact [def-weil-proper-morphism; lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. The field setting is [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. The preservation assertion for $Lf^*$ in [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors] applies to every condensed $\Lambda$ and to our $k$-morphism $g$; it therefore takes $\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$ into $\Dbc(Y',\Lambda)$. Via the two category equalities this is the required preservation of $\Dctf$. Pullback here is the ambient, uncompleted inverse image of step 1.

*Localizing closures.* Apply [det-proper-image-localizing-principle] with $\mathcal T=D(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$, $\mathcal T'=D(Y'_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$, $F=Lg^*$, $\mathcal G=\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ and $\mathcal G'=\Dctf(Y',\Lambda)$. Step 1 supplies exactness, small sums in both ambient categories, and their preservation; steps 2 and 3 supply $F(\mathcal G)\subseteq\mathcal G'\subseteq\Loc(\mathcal G')$. The cited statement therefore gives the asserted image of $\Loc(\mathcal G)$ and the exact, sum-preserving restriction.

The imported field setting is made explicit; unit realization is left to maintenance because this item is only a component of the proper-base-change unit.
